title: SIU clears police in death of mentally challenged man
article: The Special Investigations Unit has cleared Toronto police officers of any wrongdoing in connection with the arrest and subsequent death of 45-year-old Charles McGillivary.
Charles "Charlie" McGillivary, a mentally challenged man, was out with his mother Ann for some pizza on Aug. 1 when two officers stopped him near Bloor and Christie streets.

In the SIU report, officials state officers were responding to a 911 call at a Christie Street residence. They say the landlady of the residence complained a former tenant who had been evicted returned and refused to leave.

Officials say officers were in possession of a recent photograph of the suspect, who coincidentally resembled McGillivary. When they spotted McGillivary, believing it was the suspect in question, they called out to him, but he didn't answer, due to his disability.
When officers began to arrest McGillivary and a struggle ensued, he fell into medical distress.
"I came out of [the pizza shop] and Charlie is there, his face turning blue, his eyes are rolling. 'Look' I said, 'You're killing him,'" the man's mother, Ann McGillivary, told CityNews.
The grieving mother said her son suffered brain damage from a childhood car accident. He barely spoke, was deaf, and didn't understand why officers were arresting him.
McGillivary's death sparked outrage in his tight-knit community. Several rallies and vigils were held in his honour, with many people demanding accountability for his death.
The SIU is an arm's length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
